practiceProblems.title: While Loop
practiceProblems.description:
Loops can execute a block of code as long as a specified condition is reached.\
They are handy because they save time, reduce errors, and they make code more readable.\
The while loop loops through a block of code as long as a specified condition is true:

```kotlin
    Syntax - while (condition) {
                 // code to be executed
             }
```

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Declare a variable $a$ and initialise it to 0
- Use the syntax above to create a loop, output the following to the console
  - Print $a$ in separate lines as long as it is less than 7.
  - Increment $a$ by 1 in each iteration.

- Use the syntax above to create a loop, output the following to the console

  - Increment $a$ by 1 in each iteration.
constraints:
- $1 \leq T \leq 100$
- $1 \leq N \leq 100$
- $1 \leq M \leq N\cdot(N-1)/2$
- $1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq N$
- $u_i \neq v_i$ for each $1 \leq i \leq M$.
- The sum of $N$ over all test cases won't exceed $100$.
practiceProblems.inputFormat:
- The first line of input will contain a single integer $T$, denoting the number of test cases.
- Each test case consists of multiple lines of input.
    - The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers $N$ and $M$ — the number of vertices and edges of the graph, respectively.
    - The next $M$ lines describe the edges. The $i$-th of these $M$ lines contains two space-separated integers $u_i$ and $v_i$, denoting an edge between $u_i$ and $v_i$.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, output on a new line the number of good subgraphs of $G$, modulo $10^9 + 7$.

practiceProblems.title: Do While Loop
practiceProblems.description:
The **do..while** loop is a variant of the while loop. \
This loop will execute the code block once, before checking if the condition is true, then it will repeat the loop as long as the condition is true.

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Declare an integer variable $i$ and initialise it to 0
- Use the do..while loop to output $i$ to the console as long as $i$ is less than 6.

practiceProblems.title: For Loop
practiceProblems.description:
Often when you work with arrays, you need to loop through all of the elements.\
To loop through array elements, use the for loop together with the in operator:

for e.g. -->
```kotlin
val nums= arrayOf(1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
               for (x in nums) {
                  println(x)
               }
```

- Unlike Java and other programming languages, there is no traditional for loop in Kotlin.
- In Kotlin, the for loop is used to loop through arrays, ranges, and other things that contains a countable number of values.

This is how you loop through range
for e.g. -->
```kotlin
  for (nums in 0..5) {
                 println(nums)
              }
```
This will print numbers from 0 to 5

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Initialise a variable $n$ and accept a user defined input from the console
- Output "Kotlin" to the console $n$ number of times.

practiceProblems.title: Continue Statement
practiceProblems.description:
Recall that '**break**' exit the loop entirely when its condition was met - ignoring all subsequent iterations. \
The '**continue**' statement skips one iteration (in the loop), if a specified condition occurs, and continues with the next iteration in the loop.

### Task
Write a program that does the following
- Declare a variable $n$ and set it to a user defined input
- Output to the console a series of numbers from 0 to 12 with the following condition
  - Skips the number inserted by the user.

practiceProblems.title: For Each Loop
practiceProblems.description:
In Kotlin, there is no specific foreach loop like in some other programming languages.\
Instead, Kotlin provides a more versatile and concise way to iterate over elements of collections, including arrays, lists, sets, and more.\
You can use the *'for'* loop with the *'in'* keyword to achieve the same functionality as a *'foreach'* loop.

      syntax -   
```kotlin
                 for (element in collection) {
                    // Code to be executed for each element
                 }
```


       e.g:      
```kotlin
                 val numbers = arrayOf(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
                 // Using for loop to iterate over array elements
                 for (number in numbers) {
                    println(number)
                 }
```

In this example, we create an array numbers with integers and use the for loop to iterate over each element of the array. The loop iterates over the collection of elements (array elements, in this case) and assigns the current element to the variable number during each iteration. Then, we print the value of number.

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Create an array $num$ which has the integers - 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80
- Output to the console the following
  - All the elements of the given array in separate lines
  - Use the "**for**" loop syntax defined above
